subject: VARC + DILR + QA
schema_note: Keyed by topic_id (matches cat_syllabus.json). Fields: concepts, formulas, methods, traps, hard_archetypes, banned_easy_templates, out_of_scope. CAT mixes MCQ and TITA items; 'hard_archetypes' reflects CAT's characteristic multi-step/ambiguity-heavy item design rather than JEE-style symbolic proofs.

concepts: Author's tone, stance and rhetorical purpose
Implied meaning and inference beyond the literal sentence
Structure of an abstract/argumentative passage (thesis, counter-argument, synthesis)
methods: Read for the passage's central argument and author's attitude on a first pass, before hunting for specific-detail answers
Eliminate options that are true-but-not-stated or that over-extend the passage's actual claim
traps: Choosing an option that is factually plausible but not actually supported by the passage text
Confusing the author's reported view of someone else's position with the author's own view
hard_archetypes: Inference question where every option paraphrases part of the passage but only one captures the full logical implication
Tone/attitude question requiring synthesis of cues spread across the whole passage
banned_easy_templates: Direct 'which of the following is stated in the passage' with the answer in one obvious sentence
out_of_scope: Passages requiring outside domain expertise beyond what the passage itself supplies

concepts: Fact-retrieval vs application-based RC questions
Passage summary and title selection
Vocabulary-in-context for domain-specific (business/science) terms
methods: Separate 'what does the passage say' questions from 'what can be inferred/applied' questions before choosing a strategy
For title/summary questions, check that the chosen option covers the full scope of the passage, not just one paragraph
traps: Selecting a summary option that is accurate for only part of the passage (too narrow)
Selecting a summary option that goes beyond what the passage actually covers (too broad)
hard_archetypes: Application question requiring the reader to extend the passage's argument to a new, unstated scenario
Passage with a shift in argument midway, where a naive reader would answer based on only the first half
banned_easy_templates: Direct fact-lookup question answerable from a single unambiguous sentence
out_of_scope: Highly technical scientific/economic content beyond general-reader business-journalism level

concepts: Mandatory pair identification (sentences that must be adjacent)
Logical and chronological sequencing
Pronoun/referent and transition-word linkage between sentences
methods: Find the most obvious mandatory pair (linked by pronoun or clear cause-effect) before attempting the full sequence
Identify the opening sentence by elimination (sentences with 'this'/'it'/'however' rarely open a paragraph)
traps: Assuming the sentence that sounds most general must be the opener without checking for an unresolved pronoun
Locking in a sequence too early instead of verifying it reads coherently start to finish
hard_archetypes: 5-6 sentence jumble with two plausible mandatory pairs, only one of which fits the full sequence
Jumble where the topic sentence is deliberately not the most 'obvious' opener
banned_easy_templates: 3-sentence jumble with only one possible non-trivial order
out_of_scope: Jumbles requiring outside factual knowledge to sequence (should be resolvable from internal logic alone)

concepts: Distinguishing a true summary from a restatement, an example, or an over/under-generalisation
Identifying the paragraph's central idea vs supporting details
methods: Identify the paragraph's core claim first, then check which option best compresses that claim without adding or dropping scope
Eliminate options that merely repeat a supporting detail as if it were the main point
traps: Picking an option that captures one supporting example rather than the paragraph's actual main idea
Picking an option that adds an inference not actually present in the paragraph
hard_archetypes: Paragraph with two closely related ideas, where the correct summary must balance both without favouring either
banned_easy_templates: Very short paragraph with an obvious one-line restatement
out_of_scope: Summary questions requiring outside knowledge of the topic beyond the paragraph given

concepts: Thematic coherence of a paragraph (odd-one-out)
Logical continuation/conclusion for an incomplete paragraph
methods: For odd-sentence-out, check each sentence against the paragraph's single unifying theme, not just topical similarity
For para completion, identify the paragraph's trajectory (argument direction) before picking the concluding sentence
traps: Eliminating a sentence for being topically different when it is actually the concluding/linking sentence
Picking a technically true but tonally mismatched conclusion sentence
hard_archetypes: Paragraph where the 'odd' sentence is topically related but breaks the logical flow/argument direction
banned_easy_templates: Paragraph with one sentence in an obviously unrelated subject area
out_of_scope: Grammar-error-based odd-one-out (CAT's version is theme/logic-based, not grammar-based)

concepts: Reading a single table/bar/line/pie chart accurately
Percentage share, ratio and period-over-period growth-rate calculations
methods: Scan the chart's axes/legend fully before reading any question, to avoid mis-reading units
Pre-compute totals/row-column sums once, and reuse them across the set's multiple questions
traps: Misreading a dual-axis chart (two different scales on left/right y-axis)
Confusing percentage-point change with percentage change
hard_archetypes: Question requiring a ratio-of-ratios or a weighted-average computed across multiple rows of the table
banned_easy_templates: Direct single-cell lookup with no calculation
out_of_scope: Sets requiring statistical techniques (regression, standard deviation) beyond arithmetic manipulation

concepts: Combining information from two or more linked sources (table+chart, or two tables) into one working dataset
Caselet-to-table conversion from a text-based data description
methods: Before answering any question, build a single consolidated table/grid from all the given sources
In text caselets, extract every numeric constraint into a table first, only then attempt to fill gaps
traps: Answering from only one of the two linked sources when the question actually needs both combined
Missing an implicit constraint stated in the caselet's prose rather than its explicit data
hard_archetypes: Caselet with several missing values that must be deduced from consistency constraints across sources before any question can be answered
banned_easy_templates: Single-source caselet with no cross-referencing needed (belongs under CD01 instead)
out_of_scope: Sets requiring domain expertise (finance/statistics formulas) beyond what's stated in the caselet

concepts: Linear and circular seating arrangement logic
Scheduling/sequencing with day, slot or order constraints
methods: Draw the arrangement skeleton (row/circle/timeline) before placing any entity
Place the most constrained entity (fewest valid positions) first, then propagate remaining constraints
traps: Forgetting to distinguish 'facing the centre' vs 'facing outward' in a circular arrangement's left/right sense
Missing an indirect constraint implied by combining two separate given clues
hard_archetypes: Arrangement with multiple valid partial solutions that only converge to one final arrangement after combining all clues together
banned_easy_templates: Arrangement solvable by placing clues in the order given with no backtracking needed
out_of_scope: 3D or multi-dimensional arrangement puzzles beyond linear/circular/matrix layouts

concepts: Round-robin/knockout tournament structure and points-table logic
Route/network diagrams with distance or connectivity constraints
formulas: Round-robin total matches = nC2 for n teams
methods: Build the full fixture list or points table systematically before answering a specific-match question
For network/route sets, sketch the graph and track edge weights (distances/costs) as you read the clues
traps: Assuming a knockout structure when the clues actually describe round-robin (or vice versa)
Missing an indirect route/path implied by combining two direct connections
hard_archetypes: Points-table reconstruction where several matches' results must be deduced from partial standings data
banned_easy_templates: Direct 'read the given points table' question with no deduction needed
out_of_scope: Graph-theory formal algorithms (shortest-path proofs) beyond manual route-tracing

concepts: Matrix/grid puzzles assigning multiple attributes to multiple entities
Distribution puzzles allocating a fixed quantity among entities under constraints
methods: Set up a full entity-vs-attribute grid and mark 'yes/no/maybe' as each clue is processed
For distribution puzzles, use the total-sum constraint to check partial allocations as you go
traps: Forgetting that some grid puzzles allow more than one entity to share an attribute value unless explicitly restricted
Missing a hidden numeric constraint (e.g. 'total must be even') buried in the puzzle's prose
hard_archetypes: Grid puzzle with 4+ attributes and clues that require several rounds of elimination before any cell is confirmed
banned_easy_templates: Grid puzzle solvable in a single pass with directly-stated cell values
out_of_scope: Puzzles requiring formal constraint-satisfaction algorithms rather than manual elimination

concepts: Sets that combine a data table with an explicit list of logical conditions to satisfy simultaneously
Venn-diagram/set-theory based reasoning caselets
methods: List every condition explicitly before attempting to fill in any data value, then check each candidate solution against all conditions together
For Venn-based sets, fill the diagram from the innermost (most-overlapping) region outward
traps: Satisfying most but not all conditions and mistakenly treating a partial solution as final
Double-counting an overlap region when combining set totals
hard_archetypes: Set with conditions that are individually simple but jointly restrictive enough to admit only one valid data table
banned_easy_templates: Single straightforward two-set Venn diagram with no combined-condition reasoning
out_of_scope: Sets requiring formal set-theory proofs beyond a numeric/diagrammatic solution

concepts: Divisibility rules and remainder theorems
Factors, multiples, LCM-HCF applications
Number properties (odd/even, prime, perfect square) in word problems
formulas: LCM(a,b) x HCF(a,b) = a x b
Remainder of a product/sum = product/sum of remainders (mod n)
methods: Reduce a large-number divisibility question to its last-few-digits or digit-sum property before brute-forcing
Use modular arithmetic to find remainders instead of direct division for large exponents
traps: Forgetting a negative-remainder convention mismatch when a problem expects the smallest non-negative remainder
Applying a divisibility rule for one base (10) to a different base question
hard_archetypes: Remainder-of-a-large-power numerical requiring Euler's theorem or cyclicity-of-last-digit reasoning
banned_easy_templates: Direct 'find the LCM of two small numbers' with no word-problem context
out_of_scope: Formal number-theory proofs (Euler's totient derivation) beyond applied problem-solving

concepts: Percentage change and successive percentage changes
Profit, loss, discount and marked-price relationships
Simple and compound interest, including varying compounding frequency
methods: Convert all percentage changes into multiplying factors and chain them, rather than adding percentages directly
Separate marked-price/discount problems from cost-price/profit problems before setting up the equation
traps: Adding two successive percentage changes directly instead of using the successive-change formula
Confusing profit % on cost price with profit % on selling price
hard_archetypes: Multi-step problem chaining discount, tax and profit-margin together, requiring careful factor-based tracking
banned_easy_templates: Direct 'X% of Y' calculation with no chained scenario
out_of_scope: Actuarial/finance-grade compound-interest formulas (continuous compounding) beyond discrete-period CAT-style problems

concepts: Ratio and proportion, including partnership-share problems
Averages and weighted averages
Mixtures, alligation and replacement problems
formulas: Alligation: (quantity of cheaper)/(quantity of dearer) = (dearer price - mean price)/(mean price - cheaper price)
methods: Use the alligation rule directly instead of setting up simultaneous equations for a two-component mixture
For partnership problems, convert investment x time into an equivalent-capital ratio before splitting profit
traps: Applying simple average instead of weighted/time-weighted average in a partnership or mixed-group problem
Forgetting to account for the time period in a partnership investment ratio
hard_archetypes: Successive-replacement mixture problem (repeatedly removing and replacing a fraction of a mixture)
banned_easy_templates: Direct simple-average-of-a-few-numbers question with no weighting
out_of_scope: Statistical concepts (variance, standard deviation) beyond basic averages

concepts: Relative speed (same/opposite direction), trains crossing objects
Boats and streams (upstream/downstream speed)
Time and work, including pipes-and-cisterns and combined work-rate problems
formulas: Upstream speed = b-s, Downstream speed = b+s
methods: Convert all time-work statements into a common 'work done per unit time' rate before combining
For trains/boats, always identify direction (same vs opposite/upstream vs downstream) before writing the relative-speed equation
traps: Adding times directly instead of adding rates in a combined-work problem
Forgetting to account for train length when computing crossing time for two moving trains
hard_archetypes: Multi-entity work problem with some workers leaving/joining midway, requiring a piecewise rate calculation
banned_easy_templates: Direct distance=speed×time single-object question with no relative-motion element
out_of_scope: Calculus-based rate-of-change problems (this is arithmetic rate reasoning, not differential rates)

concepts: Forming and solving linear/quadratic equations from word problems
Nature of roots (discriminant), sum/product of roots
Linear and quadratic inequalities
formulas: Discriminant D = b^2-4ac determines real/imaginary and equal/distinct roots
methods: Translate the word problem into algebraic equations methodically, defining variables explicitly before solving
Use sum/product-of-roots shortcuts instead of fully solving the quadratic when only a combination of roots is asked
traps: Forgetting to check which root is valid in context (e.g. negative age/length is invalid)
Sign errors when forming an equation directly from a word problem's 'more than'/'less than' phrasing
hard_archetypes: Word problem generating a quadratic where only one of two mathematically valid roots satisfies the real-world constraint
banned_easy_templates: Direct 'solve this quadratic equation' with no word-problem translation step
out_of_scope: Cubic/higher-degree equation general solving techniques beyond quadratic-level CAT scope

concepts: Logarithm properties and change-of-base
Surds, indices and exponential equations
Function domain/range, composition and basic graph transformations
formulas: log_a b = log_c b/log_c a (change of base)
methods: Convert a mixed-base logarithmic expression to a common base before simplifying
Reduce a surd/index equation to a common base on both sides to compare exponents directly
traps: Applying log(m+n) = log m + log n (an invalid identity) instead of the correct product rule
Forgetting the domain restriction (argument > 0) when solving a logarithmic equation
hard_archetypes: Exponential equation requiring substitution (treating a^x as a new variable) to reduce to a quadratic
banned_easy_templates: Direct 'evaluate log_2 8' with no equation-solving step
out_of_scope: Complex-number-valued logarithms, formal real-analysis treatment of functions

concepts: Arithmetic, geometric and harmonic progressions
Sum of a series, including telescoping and mixed AP-GP series
methods: Identify the progression type from the pattern of consecutive-term ratios/differences before choosing a formula
Use telescoping (writing each term as a difference) for series that don't fit standard AP/GP forms
traps: Applying the AP sum formula to a GP series or vice versa
Forgetting the |r|<1 condition before using the infinite-GP-sum formula
hard_archetypes: Series requiring the arithmetico-geometric shift-and-subtract technique to sum
banned_easy_templates: Direct 'find the nth term of a stated AP' with no summation needed
out_of_scope: Formal convergence-proof techniques for infinite series beyond the standard |r|<1 rule

concepts: Triangle properties: similarity, congruence, centres (centroid, incentre, circumcentre, orthocentre)
Circle theorems: tangent-chord angle, angle in a semicircle, power of a point
Quadrilateral and regular-polygon properties
formulas: Area of triangle = ½ base x height = √(s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)) (Heron's)
Tangent-chord angle = angle in alternate segment
methods: Identify which triangle centre or circle theorem the given configuration matches before setting up equations
Use similarity ratios directly instead of full coordinate computation when only a ratio/length is asked
traps: Confusing centroid (2:1 median ratio) with incentre/circumcentre properties
Misapplying a tangent-chord angle theorem to a secant instead of a tangent
hard_archetypes: Multi-step configuration combining a triangle's centre property with a circle's tangent/chord property
banned_easy_templates: Direct 'find the third angle of a triangle given two angles' with no theorem application
out_of_scope: Formal Euclidean-proof writing; trigonometric identities beyond what's needed for a numeric geometry answer

concepts: 2D/3D mensuration: area, perimeter, volume, surface area of standard solids
Coordinate geometry: distance, section formula, equation and slope of a line, basic locus
methods: Decompose a composite solid/figure into standard shapes before applying formulas
Use the slope/section formula directly for coordinate problems instead of a full graphical approach
traps: Using the wrong formula for a frustum (truncated cone) by treating it as a full cone
Sign errors in coordinate distance/section-formula substitution
hard_archetypes: Composite-solid volume/surface-area problem requiring subtraction of an inscribed shape from an outer one
banned_easy_templates: Direct 'find the area of a rectangle given length and breadth' with no composite step
out_of_scope: 3D coordinate geometry (vectors in space) beyond standard 2D-plane CAT-level questions

concepts: Permutations and combinations with constraints (repetition, grouping, circular arrangement)
Basic and conditional probability
Set theory word problems (union/intersection via Venn diagrams)
methods: Case-split by constraint (e.g. 'together'/'never together') before applying nCr/nPr
Draw a Venn diagram for any set-theory word problem with 2+ overlapping groups before writing equations
traps: Double-counting arrangements when items within a group are identical
Forgetting to subtract the intersection term when combining two overlapping sets
hard_archetypes: Multi-constraint arrangement/selection problem requiring several cases to be summed correctly
Conditional-probability problem requiring Bayes'-style reasoning from a word scenario
banned_easy_templates: Direct nCr evaluation with given numbers and no constraint or word-problem context
out_of_scope: Formal combinatorial-proof techniques (generating functions) beyond applied CAT-level counting
